visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 presents the outcome count, combinations, winning cases, and final 93/256 with consistently correct diagrams, while Lesson 1 includes correct final numbers but has misleading or incorrect visuals such as a flawed binomial formula, nonsensical coin labels/decorations, and a bar/donut summary whose relative sizes conflict with the stated 36% vs 64% split.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons have absent gate specs and absent plan JSON, so neither shows any functional gates or checkpoints that render questions or accept input.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has coherent, natural narration with only minor wording defects like 'wave' instead of 'way,' while Lesson 2 has no transcript available and therefore provides no assessable narration quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 at least provides a narration transcript, but it lacks beat/timing and visual cue data needed to verify sync, while Lesson 2 provides no transcript or timing data at all, making it even less assessable for narration-visual alignment.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly solves the problem and explains the binomial/counting approach clearly despite a slightly imprecise general formula statement, whereas Lesson 2 has no available instructional content to verify or learn from.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has consistently larger, more legible text, centered and visually rich layouts with coherent doodle styling, whereas Lesson 2 is very sparse with tiny serif text pushed to the left, excessive empty black space, and a much less polished slide composition.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner. Four agents favored Lesson 1, including very high-confidence wins in concept accuracy, narration quality, and polish, plus a lower-confidence sync advantage. Lesson 2 won visual accuracy with high confidence, due to cleaner/correcter diagrams and outcome visuals, and interactivity was a true tie because neither lesson had functional gates or checkpoints. Up-weighting confidence still favors Lesson 1 because its strengths are broader and include the core instructional dimensions, while Lesson 2’s main advantage is limited to visual accuracy.
